animals.didYouKnow: The female keeps the eggs in her body until they hatch, then gives birth to young live cockroaches.

animals.recognition: Small, shiny oval beetle that circles rapidly on the surface of the water.
animals.didYouKnow: Its short antennas detect surface disturbances produced around it.

animals.recognition: Wings erect at rest and long filaments at the end of the abdomen.
animals.didYouKnow: Its larvae can dig into the sediments and thus participate in the rearrangement of the bottom of watercourses.

animals.recognition: Dark wings barred with red-orange and punctuated with white at the tips.
animals.didYouKnow: It can feed on very ripe fruits and sap, in addition to flower nectar.

animals.recognition: Very colorful crustacean with pedunculated eyes and massive front appendages.
animals.didYouKnow: His blow can create a cavitation bubble; the collapse of this bubble adds a disturbance to that of the initial shock.

animals.recognition: Light spiral shell with brown bands and numerous tentacles without suckers.
animals.didYouKnow: It expels water through an adjustable siphon, which allows it to propel itself and direct its movements.

animals.recognition: Blue marine slug with black lines and yellow-orange border.
animals.didYouKnow: It feeds on marine sponges from which it takes tissue using its oral apparatus.

animals.recognition: Small light crab covered with very contrasting dark bands.
animals.didYouKnow: Its legs have adaptations that help it cling between the spines of sea urchins.

animals.recognition: Small crab with geometric patterns, sometimes carrying an anemone in each claw.
animals.didYouKnow: Its very specialized claws become less adapted to certain classic dietary manipulations of other crabs.

animals.recognition: Orange or light fleshy colony divided into finger-like lobes.
animals.didYouKnow: Each small polyp in the colony bears eight feathery tentacles that capture food particles.

animals.recognition: Numerous feathery arms radiating around a small central disc.
animals.didYouKnow: She can move by crawling with her appendages and sometimes swim using her arm movements.

animals.recognition: Green slug whose lateral expansions give a leaf shape.
animals.didYouKnow: The young must consume a particular algae to acquire the chloroplasts responsible for part of their green color.

animals.recognition: Two colored spiral crowns protrude from a tube attached to the substrate.
animals.didYouKnow: It can very quickly retract its crowns into its tube when a shadow or a disturbance announces danger.

animals.recognition: Segmented worm with white tufts on the sides.
animals.didYouKnow: Its bristles can become detached from the skin of an animal that touches it and cause significant irritation.

animals.recognition: Pale elongated salamander with small legs and external gills.
animals.didYouKnow: Its life cycle is slow and individuals can live for several decades in favorable conditions.

animals.recognition: Very flattened toad with a triangular head and rough brownish skin.
animals.didYouKnow: The fingers of its front paws carry small sensory branches useful for exploring the bottom.

animals.recognition: Small green frog with fingers equipped with discs and a translucent ventral surface.
animals.didYouKnow: Its disc-shaped fingers help it to hold on to leaves in humid vegetation.

animals.recognition: Legless amphibian with a ringed body reminiscent of a worm.
animals.didYouKnow: It lives mainly buried in the ground, where it searches for small invertebrates.

animals.recognition: Elongated velvety body with many pairs of small fleshy legs.
animals.didYouKnow: In this Australian species, the young are born alive, while other onychophores lay eggs.

animals.recognition: Domed horseshoe carapace and long caudal tip.
animals.didYouKnow: The tail serves in particular as a lever to turn itself right side up when turned over.

animals.recognition: Abdomen of the female striped yellow, black and white.
animals.didYouKnow: The female wraps her eggs in a silk cocoon which can spend the bad season in the vegetation.

animals.recognition: Brown spider whose body can appear silver underwater.
animals.didYouKnow: Its hairs retain a layer of air around the abdomen when it dives.

animals.recognition: Green frog with very long, widely webbed fingers.
animals.didYouKnow: Its clutches develop in moss nests associated with vegetation above the water.

animals.recognition: Very large amphibian with a flattened head and strongly wrinkled dark skin.
animals.didYouKnow: A male can guard a nesting cavity and fan the eggs through the movements of his tail.

animals.recognition: The male has large branched mandibles reminiscent of antlers.
animals.didYouKnow: Females have mandibles that are shorter than those of large males, but capable of pinching effectively.
